He is widely honored in central Europe as patron of those who fight fires.
5-4.desc: Holy Martyr Florian, a Roman officer drowned for his faith at Lorch in present-day Austria.
5-4.name: Florian the Martyr

5-4.bio:
The synaxarion records that Venerable Hilarion lived a life of asceticism and was granted the gift of working wonders, reposing in peace. Beyond this little has been preserved.

He is commemorated on May 4 together with the other saints of the day.
5-4.desc: Venerable Hilarion the Wonderworker, an ascetic honored in the Greek synaxarion.
5-4.name: Hilarion the Wonderworker

5-5.bio:
The Holy Great Martyr Irene lived in the early centuries of the Church. According to tradition she was the daughter of a pagan ruler and came to faith in Christ in her youth, receiving in baptism the name Irene, which means peace. Confessing the Lord openly, she endured many tortures with courage, and her endurance drew multitudes to belief.

She is honored as one of the great women martyrs of the Church, and many churches across the Greek world bear her name. Her feast on May 5 is the beloved name day of all who bear the name Irene.
5-5.name: Irene the Great Martyr

5-5.bio:
Ephraim was born in Trikala in the late fourteenth century and became a monk at the Monastery of the Annunciation on Mount Amomon near Nea Makri in Attica. When Turkish raiders attacked the monastery, tradition relates that he was tortured for months and finally killed, nailed to a mulberry tree, in 1426.

His relics were discovered in 1950 after a nun of the monastery was guided to the spot in prayer, and many healings have been attributed to his intercession since.
5-5.desc: Great Martyr Ephraim the Wonderworker of Nea Makri, monk of Mount Amomon martyred by the Turks.
5-5.name: Ephraim of Nea Makri

5-5.bio:
Euthymios was bishop of Madytos on the Thracian shore of the Hellespont, traditionally placed in the tenth century. He was renowned for his charity and for the wonders worked through his prayers both in life and after his death.

His relics were treasured in Madytos and he is remembered on May 5.
5-5.desc: Saint Euthymios the Wonderworker, Bishop of Madytos in Thrace.
5-5.name: Euthymios of Madytos

5-5.bio:
Irenaeus, Irene and Peregrinus were Christians of Thessalonica who were put to death for their faith, according to the synaxarion by fire. They are honored together on the same day as the Great Martyr Irene.

Nothing further of their story has been preserved.
5-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Irenaeus, Irene and Peregrinus, who suffered at Thessalonica.
5-5.name: Irenaeus, Irene and Peregrinus of Thessalonica

5-5.bio:
The synaxarion honors the martyrs Neophytos, Gaius and Gaianos on May 5, recording that they gave their lives for Christ. The place and time of their martyrdom are not preserved.

They are commemorated together with the Great Martyr Irene.
5-5.desc: Holy Martyrs Neophytos, Gaius and Gaianos.
5-5.name: Neophytos, Gaius and Gaianos

5-5.bio:
Martha lived in Monemvasia in the Peloponnese and, after her widowhood, devoted herself to prayer, fasting and works of mercy, tradition placing her around the tenth century. She is remembered for her humility and her care for the needy.

She reposed in peace and is honored locally on May 5.
5-5.desc: Venerable Martha of Monemvasia, a woman ascetic of the Peloponnese.
5-5.name: Martha of Monemvasia

5-6.bio:
The Righteous Job lived in the land of Uz in the age of the patriarchs, a man blameless and upright who feared God and turned away from evil. Tested by the loss of his wealth, his children, and his health, he refused to curse God, saying that the Lord gave and the Lord has taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord.

His patience under affliction has comforted the suffering in every generation, and the Church reads his book in Holy Week, seeing in the righteous sufferer a foreshadowing of Christ. He is commemorated on May 6.
5-6.name: Job the Long-Suffering

5-6.bio:
Seraphim was born in Boeotia in the sixteenth century and became a monk in the region of Helicon. After years of solitude he founded the Monastery of the Transfiguration on Mount Dombou near Levadeia, gathering many disciples.

He reposed in 1602 and is venerated throughout Boeotia as a wonderworker.
5-6.desc: Venerable Seraphim of Levadeia, founder of the Monastery of the Savior on Mount Dombou.
5-6.name: Seraphim of Dombou

5-6.bio:
Sophia Chotokouridou was born in Pontus in 1883 and came to Greece with the exchange of populations. She settled at the Monastery of the Nativity of the Theotokos at Kleisoura in western Macedonia, where she lived for decades in the fireplace of the church, in poverty, cold and continual prayer.

Many came to her for counsel and she was known for her gift of insight and her love of the poor. She reposed in 1974 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in 2011.
5-6.desc: Venerable Sophia the Ascetic of Kleisoura, the Panagia's beloved of Macedonia.
5-6.name: Sophia of Kleisoura

5-6.bio:
Barbaros was a soldier in the army of Julian the Apostate who, according to the synaxarion, prevailed in single combat and was then discovered to be a Christian. He refused to sacrifice to the gods and was tortured and beheaded, together with Bacchus, Callimachus and Dionysius, who confessed Christ on witnessing his steadfastness.

They are commemorated on May 6.
5-6.desc: Holy Martyr Barbaros the Soldier, with Bacchus, Callimachus and Dionysius, who suffered under Julian the Apostate.
5-6.name: Barbaros the Soldier

5-6.bio:
Benedicta was a nun of a Roman monastery in the time of Saint Benedict, remembered for her purity of life. Tradition relates that Saint Benedict foresaw her death and that she reposed in peace after a holy life.

She is commemorated on May 6.
5-6.desc: Venerable Benedicta of Rome, a nun of the sixth century.
5-6.name: Benedicta the Roman

5-6.bio:
Job was born in Galicia in the sixteenth century and became a monk in his youth. He was later abbot of the Lavra of Pochaev, where he strengthened the community, printed Orthodox books and defended the faith against the Unia.

He reposed in 1651 and is remembered on his name-day, the feast of the righteous Job.
5-6.desc: Venerable Job, abbot and wonderworker of Pochaev, defender of Orthodoxy in western Rus.
5-6.name: Job of Pochaev

5-7.bio:
The Holy Martyr Akakios was a young soldier from Cappadocia who suffered for Christ at the beginning of the fourth century, during the persecutions of the pagan emperors. Denounced as a Christian, he confessed the Lord boldly before his commanders, endured imprisonment and torture without wavering, and was beheaded at Byzantium.

He was venerated there from early times, and a church was raised in his honor in the city that became Constantinople. His faithful confession is kept in memory by the Church on May 7.
5-7.name: Akakios of Cappadocia

5-7.bio:
On the morning of May 7 in the year 351, during the reign of the Emperor Constantius, a great Cross of light appeared in the sky above Jerusalem, stretching from Golgotha to the Mount of Olives. It was seen by the whole city and lasted for several hours.

Saint Cyril of Jerusalem described the event in a letter to the emperor, and the Church has kept its memory ever since.
5-7.desc: Commemoration of the luminous Cross that appeared in the sky over Jerusalem in the reign of Constantius.
5-7.name: Sign of the Cross over Jerusalem

5-7.bio:
Kodratos was a Christian of Nicomedia who, during the persecution of Decius, openly encouraged the imprisoned believers and confessed his own faith before the governor. He was tortured in several cities of Asia Minor and finally beheaded.

Tradition relates that many who saw his endurance believed and suffered with him.
5-7.desc: Holy Martyr Kodratos (Quadratus) and those with him, who suffered at Nicomedia under Decius.
5-7.name: Kodratos and Companions

5-7.bio:
Nilus was born in the Peloponnese in the sixteenth century and became a monk on Mount Athos, where he lived as a hermit in a cave near the Great Lavra. After his repose in 1651 myrrh flowed from his relics in such abundance that it ran down the cliff to the sea.

His relics were found in 1815, and this day commemorates that finding; his main feast is November 12.
5-7.desc: Finding of the relics of Venerable Nilus the Myrrhstreamer of Mount Athos.
5-7.name: Nilus the Myrrhstreamer

5-7.bio:
Nilus was born in the fifteenth century and became a monk of the Kirillo-Belozersky Monastery. He travelled to Mount Athos, where he learned the hesychast tradition, and on his return founded a small skete on the river Sora, living in poverty and continual prayer.

He taught that monasteries should own no villages and wrote a Rule of skete life. He reposed in 1508.
5-7.desc: Venerable Nilus of Sora, founder of skete life in Russia and teacher of non-possession.
5-7.name: Nilus of Sora

5-7.bio:
John was abbot of the Psycha Monastery in Constantinople in the ninth century. For his defense of the holy icons he was exiled and suffered much at the hands of the Iconoclast emperors.

He returned after the restoration of the icons and reposed in peace, honored as a confessor.
5-7.desc: Venerable John the Confessor, abbot of the Psycha Monastery in Constantinople during the Iconoclast persecution.
5-7.name: John Psychaites

5-7.bio:
Alexis Toth was born in 1854 to a Carpatho-Rusyn family in what is now Slovakia and was ordained a Greek Catholic priest. Sent to Minneapolis, he was rejected by the Latin archbishop, and in 1891 he and his parish returned to the Orthodox Church.

He spent the rest of his life bringing thousands of Rusyn immigrants back to Orthodoxy across the United States, reposing in 1909. He was glorified in 1994.
5-7.desc: Saint Alexis Toth, confessor and defender of Orthodoxy in America.
5-7.name: Alexis Toth

5-8.bio:
St. John the Theologian, the Beloved Disciple, was the son of Zebedee and brother of James, called from his nets by the Lord. He leaned on the breast of Christ at the Mystical Supper, stood by the Cross when the others had fled, and received the Theotokos into his care. He wrote the Fourth Gospel, three Epistles, and the Revelation.

According to tradition he lived to a great age in Ephesus, teaching his disciples above all to love one another. One of the few saints the Church names Theologian, he is commemorated on May 8 and at his repose on September 26.
5-8.desc: Holy Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian, the Beloved Disciple.
5-8.name: John the Theologian

5-8.bio:
Arsenios was a learned Roman deacon chosen by the Emperor Theodosius as tutor to his sons Arcadius and Honorius. Praying for guidance, he heard a voice telling him to flee from men and be saved, and he departed secretly for the desert of Scetis in Egypt.

There he lived in silence and unceasing tears for many years, avoiding visitors and saying that he had often repented of speaking but never of silence. He reposed around the year 450 and is one of the great fathers of the Egyptian desert.
5-8.desc: Venerable Arsenios the Great, tutor of emperors who fled to the Egyptian desert.
5-8.name: Arsenios the Great

5-8.bio:
The synaxarion records the martyr Augustina, who suffered for Christ in Constantinople. The circumstances of her martyrdom have not been preserved.

She is commemorated on May 8.
5-8.name: Augustina the Martyr

5-8.bio:
Arsenios was the founder of the Monastery of the Theotokos of Varnakova in the mountains of Nafpaktia in central Greece, traditionally in the eleventh century. He gathered a brotherhood there and established a rule of common life.

He is honored on the feast of his namesake Arsenios the Great.
5-8.desc: Venerable Arsenios, founder of the Monastery of Varnakova in Nafpaktia.
5-8.name: Arsenios of Varnakova

5-8.bio:
Little is recorded of Venerable Miles beyond his life of asceticism and his labors as a writer of hymns. The synaxarion honors him on May 8.

He reposed in peace.
5-8.desc: Venerable Miles the Hymnographer, an ascetic and composer of church hymns.
5-8.name: Miles the Hymnographer

5-8.bio:
Cassian was a monk of the Kiev Caves Lavra who shut himself in a cell in the Far Caves and gave himself to prayer, fasting and obedience. The paterikon of the Lavra remembers him for humility and love of labor.

His relics rest in the Far Caves; he is placed in the thirteenth or fourteenth century.
5-8.desc: Venerable Cassian the Recluse of the Far Caves of Kiev.
5-8.name: Cassian the Recluse of the Kiev Caves

5-9.bio:
The Holy Prophet Isaiah prophesied in Jerusalem in the eighth century before Christ. Beholding the Lord upon His throne, with the seraphim crying Holy, Holy, Holy, he was cleansed by a burning coal and sent to call the people to repentance. His book is filled with prophecies of the Messiah, of the virgin who would conceive, and of the suffering servant wounded for our transgressions.

For the clarity of these prophecies he is called the evangelist among the prophets, and tradition holds that he died a martyr. He is commemorated on May 9.
5-9.name: Isaiah the Prophet

5-9.bio:
Christopher was a man of great stature from the region of Lycia who came to faith and was baptized with the name Christopher, the Christ-bearer. Tradition relates that his appearance was so fearsome that pagans fled from him, yet he brought many to Christ by his gentleness and the wonders worked through his prayers.

Under the Emperor Decius he was arrested, and the two women sent to seduce him were instead converted. After many tortures he was beheaded around the year 250. He is invoked as a protector of travelers.
5-9.desc: Great Martyr Christopher of Lycia, the Christ-bearer, beheaded under Decius.
5-9.name: Christopher the Great Martyr

5-9.bio:
Nicholas was an officer of the Byzantine army stationed in Thessaly in the tenth century. Withdrawing to the forests of Vounena near Larisa, he lived as an ascetic with a small band of companions.

When barbarian raiders overran the region, his companions were killed and Nicholas, refusing to renounce Christ, was pierced with a lance beneath an oak tree. His relics are venerated in Thessaly and he is invoked for healing.
5-9.desc: Holy Martyr Nicholas the New of Vounena in Thessaly, a soldier who became an ascetic and was slain by invaders.
5-9.name: Nicholas of Vounena

5-9.bio:
Hieronymos was born in Cappadocia in 1871 and became a monk at the Monastery of Simonos Petra on Mount Athos. Sent to serve at the monastery's dependency of the Ascension in Athens, he spent decades there as confessor and spiritual father to countless people.

He was known for his humility, his gift of discernment and his love for the poor. He reposed in 1957 and was glorified by the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
5-9.desc: Venerable Hieronymos of Simonopetra, elder of Mount Athos and Athens.
5-9.name: Hieronymos of Simonopetra

5-9.bio:
The synaxarion honors the holy women Aquilina and Kallinike on May 9, recording that they suffered for Christ. The details of their martyrdom are not preserved.

They are commemorated together with the Prophet Isaiah and the Great Martyr Christopher.
5-9.desc: Holy Women Martyrs Aquilina and Kallinike.
5-9.name: Aquilina and Kallinike

5-9.bio:
Epimachos and Gordianos were Christians of Rome who confessed the faith during the persecutions of the fourth century and were beheaded. Their relics were buried together on the Via Latina.

They are commemorated on May 9.
5-9.desc: Holy Martyrs Epimachos and Gordianos, who suffered at Rome.
5-9.name: Epimachos and Gordianos

5-9.bio:
Maximos confessed Christ during the persecution of Maximian and, according to tradition, lost an eye and the use of a leg under torture. Surviving the persecution, he became Bishop of Jerusalem in the fourth century and took part in the Council of Nicaea.

He was a friend and defender of Saint Athanasios and reposed in peace around the year 350.
5-9.desc: Saint Maximos the Confessor, Bishop of Jerusalem, who bore the marks of persecution into his episcopate.
5-9.name: Maximos of Jerusalem
